records.name: Ādi
records.label: Adi
records.counting: Beat + 3 finger counts (laghu), then beat + wave (drutam), then beat + wave (drutam).
records.notes: The most common tala in Carnatic kritis; structurally it is chatusra-jati Tripuṭa tala. 8 aksharas per cycle, grouped 4+2+2. Desādi and Madhyādi are eduppu (starting-point) variants of this same structure, not separate talas.

records.name: Rūpaka
records.label: Rupaka
records.counting: Beat + wave (drutam), then beat + 3 finger counts (laghu).
records.notes: As commonly counted in kriti attributions, Rūpaka has 6 aksharas (drutam + chatusra laghu). Many performers feel it informally as a 3-beat cycle, but the formal akshara count used in notation is 6.

records.name: Miśra Cāpu
records.label: Misra Chapu
records.counting: Clap through a group of 3 counts, then clap through a group of 4 counts. Chapu talas are counted by claps only, with no waves (no drutam/laghu anga symbols used).
records.notes: 7-akshara cycle. Some texts and teaching lineages write the grouping as 3+4, others as 4+3 (i.e., which clap falls first varies by tradition) — both describe the same 7-count cycle.

records.name: Khaṇḍa Cāpu
records.label: Khanda Chapu
records.counting: Clap through a group of 2 counts, then clap through a group of 3 counts.
records.notes: 5-akshara cycle, counted purely by claps like all chapu talas. Some traditions reverse the grouping to 3+2. Good early tala for practicing asymmetric (non-4/8-beat) counting.

records.name: Dēśādi
records.label: Desadi
records.angas: laghu(4) + drutam(2) + drutam(2) [Ādi tala structure; sahitya eduppu at akshara 4]
records.counting: Count Ādi tala normally (beat + 3 finger counts, beat + wave, beat + wave); the first sahitya syllable lands after 1.5 beats have elapsed, i.e., on the 4th akshara of the cycle.
records.notes: Dēśādi is NOT a separate tala structure — it is Ādi tala (8 aksharas, laghu+drutam+drutam) distinguished only by its eduppu: the sung syllable begins after 3 aksharas (1.5 beats) have passed. Contrast with plain Ādi (eduppu on beat 1) and Madhyādi (eduppu at the 8-akshara cycle's midpoint).

records.name: Madhyādi
records.label: Madhyadi
records.angas: laghu(4) + drutam(2) + drutam(2) [Ādi tala structure; sahitya eduppu at akshara 5]
records.counting: Count Ādi tala normally (beat + 3 finger counts, beat + wave, beat + wave); the first sahitya syllable lands after 2 full beats (4 aksharas) have elapsed, i.e., on the 5th akshara — exactly the midpoint of the 8-akshara cycle.
records.notes: Like Dēśādi, Madhyādi is an eduppu convention within Ādi tala, not a distinct anga structure. 'Madhya' (middle) refers to the sahitya starting at the exact midpoint of the avartana, after the laghu and first drutam have completed.

records.name: Aṭa
records.label: Ata
records.counting: Beat + 4 finger counts (laghu), beat + 4 finger counts (laghu), beat + wave (drutam), beat + wave (drutam).
records.notes: As used in kriti attributions, Aṭa tala is khanda-jati: two khanda laghus (5 each) followed by two drutams, 14 aksharas per cycle. Rare in the kriti repertoire — most of what looks long is Adi at a slow pace. All five Pancharatna kritis are in Adi, not Ata.

records.name: Jhampā
records.label: Jhampa
records.counting: Beat + 6 finger counts (laghu), then beat + wave (drutam), then a single beat with no wave (anudrutam).
records.notes: As used in kriti attributions, Jhampa tala is misra-jati: a 7-count laghu, a drutam, and a lone anudrutam. 10 aksharas per cycle. The anudrutam anga (a bare single beat) appears only in this tala among common kriti talas, making it useful for drilling that anga.

records.name: Tripuṭa
records.label: Triputa
records.counting: Beat + 2 finger counts (laghu), then beat + wave (drutam), then beat + wave (drutam).
records.notes: As used plainly in kriti attributions, Tripuṭa tala is tisra-jati (3+2+2 = 7 aksharas). If the same laghu+drutam+drutam skeleton is performed in chatusra jati (4+2+2 = 8) it becomes Ādi tala — the two talas share one anga structure across different jatis.

records.name: Ēka
records.label: Eka
records.counting: Beat + 3 finger counts — a single laghu, repeating each cycle.
records.notes: The simplest of the sapta talas: one chatusra laghu, 4 aksharas per cycle. Useful as a first tala for internalizing laghu counting before combining angas.

records.name: Mātya
records.label: Matya
records.counting: Beat + 3 finger counts (laghu), then beat + wave (drutam), then beat + 3 finger counts (laghu).
records.notes: 10-akshara cycle in chatusra jati (4+2+4). Less frequently seen in kriti attributions than Ādi, Rūpaka, or the chapu talas, but appears in works of several composers.
